_law: A CLASSIFICATION IS NOT A BASELINE. Every entry here is a constant argued to be NOT AN OPINION — there is no organization that could sensibly hold a different view of it — and every entry carries the argument. The guard REFUSES an entry without a real reason or with an unknown kind, and it can never add one: only a person editing this file by hand can, and the only thing --write may do is REMOVE an entry whose constant no longer exists.
_why: CLAUDE.md law 6 says opinions become knobs. It does NOT say every number becomes a knob. A provider ceiling we do not own, a defensive cap that exists so one bad payload cannot take the process down, the feel of a hover delay, and a constant of an algorithm are not choices an organization gets to make — turning them into knobs would put 228 controls in front of people that mean nothing to their business and bury the ones that do. scripts/settings-hardcoded-allowlist.json is the DEBT list: values that ARE opinions and have not been converted yet. This file is the opposite: values that were looked at and are not opinions at all. A line belongs in exactly one of them.

_kinds.protocol: A wire, transport or provider bound we do not own — a payload byte ceiling, a filename length a mail client accepts, a provider API maximum. Raising it would be refused by the thing on the other end.
_kinds.defensive-cap: A ceiling that exists so one runaway input cannot take a process, a browser tab or a sweep down. It is not how much of their data an organization may have; it is what one call may carry at once.
_kinds.ui-timing: Interaction feel — a hover delay, a typeahead window, an input debounce, a dwell. Owned by the design system so every surface feels the same, never by one customer.
_kinds.algorithmic: A constant of the algorithm itself — a recursion depth, a minimum number of rows for a method to mean anything, an epsilon, a scoring weight. Changing it changes what the code IS, not what the organization wants.
_kinds.resolver-cache: How long a resolved value is trusted inside one process before it is re-read. An implementation detail of the resolver, and in several cases of the knob resolver itself — which cannot be configured by a knob without asking the registry how often to ask the registry.
_kinds.operational-timeout: How long our own code waits on our own infrastructure before it gives up and says so. The organization feels the failure, never the number.

_how: pnpm check:settings-hardcoded --write removes entries whose constant is gone. To ADD one, edit this file by hand and write the sentence: say what the value is bounded BY, and why no organization could hold a different view of it. If you cannot write that sentence, it is an opinion — register it in platform.feature_knob and read it through the resolution API.
_classified_by: SETTINGS-3 — each entry read against ~30 lines of its own surrounding source, never from its name.

entries.name: SHAPE_CACHE_MS
entries.reason: How long ONE catalog answer is trusted before it is re-read: whether billing.customer carries organization_id yet (REC-62). It is not a value about anybody's business — it is the staleness window on a `limit 0` probe of the live catalog, and every organization on every database gets the same answer from it. Its bound is the DDL commit itself: the shape changes exactly once, unattended, with no redeploy, so the window has to be shorter than a person's patience on that one night and long enough that the probe costs one select per server process per half-minute. An organization holding a different view of it would be holding a view about our own migration window.

entries.name: POLL_INTERVAL_MS

entries.name: IMPACT_AGENT_PAGE_SIZE
entries.reason: Admin console page size kept safely under the server's own hard caps (max_agent_ids 500, max_principal_groups 64); pagination bounded by a real server limit, with any refusal shown verbatim.

entries.name: AUTO_ADVANCE_TOAST_MS
entries.reason: Dwell time for the auto-advance toast; UI feedback timing.

entries.name: REACH_TOAST_MS
entries.reason: How long an admin toast stays up after a mandate-reach action; UI dwell time.

entries.name: MANDATE_SEED_DEADLINE_MS
entries.reason: Explicitly bounded well under the hosting function's own 15s timeout so a slow-but-alive database still seeds the page; a measured infra constant.

entries.name: MAX_WINDOW_ROWS
entries.reason: A defensive ceiling on in-memory analytics rows processed in one window; a runaway-guard scale number, not a business-facing data limit.

entries.name: QUEUE_REFRESH_MS
entries.reason: How often an admin page-analysis queue status control re-polls; a UI freshness cadence, not a business setting.

entries.name: PAGE_INTENT_LIMIT
entries.reason: Explicitly matches the server RPC's own clamp (seo.list_page_intents clamps to 1..1000); the rollup takes the maximum the server ever allows regardless of preference.

entries.name: OUTLINE_SEARCH_DEBOUNCE_MS
entries.reason: Debounce before filtering the topic-map tree on keystroke; a standard input debounce.

entries.name: CLEAN_OUTCOME_DWELL_MS
entries.reason: How long a clean (nothing to read) bulk-outcome banner stays up before self-clearing; explicitly called 'a dwell time, not a taste' in the source.

entries.name: PAGE_SEARCH_LIMIT
entries.reason: How many page hits a merge/redirect target picker's search shows at once; framed as enough to choose from and short enough to read, a picker-readability constant.

entries.name: TOPIC_SEARCH_LIMIT
entries.reason: How many topic hits a picker's search shows at once; explicitly 'enough to choose from, short enough to read' — UI readability, not data completeness.

entries.name: TOPIC_SEARCH_LIMIT
entries.reason: How many topics a run-control picker's search offers at once; same picker-readability reasoning as the sibling topic search limit.

entries.name: INTENTS_PAGE_LIMIT
entries.reason: Explicitly matches the server RPC's own clamp (seo.list_page_intents clamps to 1..1000); the table takes the maximum the server ever allows and states a partial read rather than truncating silently.

entries.name: KNOB_RESOLVE_GRACE_MS
entries.reason: How long a caller waits for the settings ladder to resolve before falling back to the documented default; the same resolution-grace pattern used elsewhere, not itself a business setting.

entries.name: MAX_REFRESH_WINDOW_DAYS
entries.reason: Explicitly the YouTube provider's own ceiling (YouTubeRefreshRequest.validate_window caps a refresh at 90 days); nothing here could ask for more regardless of preference.

entries.name: MIN_WEIGHT
entries.reason: Floor weight in an internal method-scoring algorithm for capture-plan scheduling; a scoring constant, not a business setting.

entries.name: MAX_ATTEMPTS
entries.reason: How many times an optimistic-concurrency write re-reads and re-applies before giving up; retry plumbing, not a business preference.

entries.name: MIN_NARRATIVE_CHARS
entries.reason: Shortest narrative worth running the unfolding/ordering pass on; an algorithmic quality gate, not a business setting.

entries.name: MAX_SELECTED
entries.reason: A client-side warning mirror of the server's own enforced cost cap on shadow-inbox selections; changing it locally would not change what the server accepts.

entries.name: MAX_DESKS
entries.reason: Fixes what 'the comparison' means (pairwise, two desks) as a product/UX concept, not a fetch limit an org would tune.

entries.name: MAX_ATTEMPTS
entries.reason: How many times an optimistic-concurrency write re-reads and re-applies before giving up; the same retry plumbing pattern used elsewhere in this codebase.

entries.name: RECONNECT_BASE_MS
entries.reason: Base delay before retrying a dropped voice-interview session; retry-backoff plumbing.

entries.name: RECONNECT_MAX_MS
entries.reason: Ceiling on the same reconnect backoff as the base delay above; paired retry plumbing.

entries.name: MAX_COMMAND_WORDS
entries.reason: Longest an utterance may be and still match as a short voice command; a speech-matching heuristic, not a business setting.

entries.name: MAX_CONFIDENCE
entries.reason: Upper clamp on a Brier-score confidence value; the paired mathematical scoring bound.

entries.name: MIN_CONFIDENCE
entries.reason: Lower clamp on a Brier-score confidence value; a mathematical scoring bound, not a business preference.

entries.name: MAX_ATTEMPTS
entries.reason: How many times an optimistic-concurrency write re-reads and re-applies before giving up; the same retry plumbing pattern used elsewhere.

entries.name: INTERVIEW_HISTORY_MS
entries.reason: Measured opening-promise duration for loading interview history, same measured family as its siblings.

entries.name: INTERVIEW_OPENING_MS
entries.reason: Measured opening-promise duration for starting an interview, from the same production-measured family as the sibling opening-rate constants.

entries.name: INTERVIEW_RESUME_MS
entries.reason: Measured opening-promise duration for resuming an interview, same measured family as its siblings.

entries.name: NEW_RULEBOOK_OPENING_MS
entries.reason: Measured (not guessed) duration a 'starting' promise sentence holds before the UI switches to reporting elapsed time honestly; an engineering constant tied to real production timings.

entries.name: DUMP_URL_CAS_RETRIES
entries.reason: How many times a compare-and-swap write retries against a fresh row before surfacing a conflict; optimistic-concurrency plumbing, not a business setting.

entries.name: WRITE_DEBOUNCE_MS
entries.reason: Debounce before writing a dialog's in-progress sitting to storage; interaction-feel plumbing.

entries.name: MAX_CASES
entries.reason: Bounds a quadratic pairwise-comparison sort at roughly the point a human stops sorting a pile by hand; an algorithmic/usability bound, not a business setting.

entries.name: TRIAD_DEAL_USUAL_MS
entries.reason: Measured (not guessed) usual duration for dealing a round of cards, used only to phrase an honest waiting sentence; a production-measured engineering constant.

entries.name: RECEIPT_POLL_MS
entries.reason: Thin client poll paired with the ALB-timeout-derived wait above; polling plumbing, not a business setting.

entries.name: RECEIPT_WAIT_MS
entries.reason: Explicitly derived from the public load balancer's own 60s idle_timeout; an infra constraint, not a business preference.

entries.name: SAVED_BEFORE_CAPTURE_WINDOW_MS
entries.reason: Matches the autosave debounce plus a slow request's worst case, used only to decide whether a save is 'already the capture's own text'; a heuristic window, not a business setting.

entries.name: NEW_NOTE_ORGANIZATION_WAIT_MS
entries.reason: How long a click waits for the organization-bootstrap state before refusing; a resilience timeout, not a business setting.

entries.name: WAIT_TICK_MS
entries.reason: Minimum spacing between store-change checks so the wait doesn't become a busy-loop; engineering plumbing.

entries.name: CONTENT_SEARCH_DEBOUNCE_MS
entries.reason: Debounce before a note-body search query leaves the browser; a standard input debounce.

entries.name: RETRY_BASE_DELAY_MS
entries.reason: Starting delay of an exponential retry/backoff loop for failed note autosaves; retry plumbing, not a business setting.

entries.name: RETRY_MAX_DELAY_MS
entries.reason: Ceiling of the same exponential retry/backoff loop; paired retry plumbing.

entries.name: ATTEMPT_POLL_MS
entries.reason: Diagnostics poll used only to surface a realtime channel's own reconnect-attempt count while it is down; internal status plumbing.

entries.name: LIST_SESSION_SETTLE_MS
entries.reason: How long the first read after boot waits for the Supabase session to name the same user Redux already holds; a startup race-condition fix, not a business setting.

entries.name: INBOX_PANEL_LIMIT
entries.reason: How many notices the inbox panel shows before offering 'See all'; a display cap with the full list always reachable, not a data limit.

entries.name: INBOX_POLL_INTERVAL_MS
entries.reason: How often the notification badge re-reads while the tab is open; a lightweight UI freshness cadence, not a costed or org-tunable cadence.

entries.name: MIN_PODCAST_CONTENT_CHARS
entries.reason: A client mirror of the podcast generator's own server-side Gate 1 minimum-content check; refuses locally only what the server would deterministically reject anyway.

entries.name: HIGHLIGHT_MS
entries.reason: How long a highlight ring stays up after a deep link points at a device row; a UI attention cue, not a business setting.

entries.name: POLL_INTERVAL_MS
entries.reason: Degraded-mode poll cadence explicitly matched to its sibling devices surface so the two halves of one screen stay consistent; engineering, not a business knob.

entries.name: SCHEDULE_ROSTER_LOAD_TIMEOUT_MS
entries.reason: Abort boundary so a schedules roster load never hangs forever; a resilience timeout matching the platform's other load timeouts.

entries.name: TTL_MS
entries.reason: Short in-memory time-to-live for an unsaved generated password candidate before it is treated as stale; a security-hygiene default, not a configurable business setting.

entries.name: LIVE_REREAD_INTERVAL_MS
entries.reason: How often a running job's panel re-reads its durable rows while live; explicitly picked as the interval that reads as 'live' at low read cost, an engineering cadence.

entries.name: NUDGE_DEBOUNCE_MS
entries.reason: Coalesces a realtime notice burst into one re-read; debounce plumbing.

entries.name: MAX_PENDING
entries.reason: Bound on an in-memory navigation-handoff map so a tab navigating all day cannot grow it forever; a client memory cap.

entries.name: SEED_TTL_MS
entries.reason: How long an in-memory page-navigation name handoff stays usable for one client navigation; a short-lived transient cache TTL, not a business setting.

entries.name: UNDO_TOAST_MS
entries.reason: How long an 'Undo' offer stays up after a singleton panel replaced another record; UI dwell time.

entries.name: TICK_MS
entries.reason: Clock tick interval powering every relative-time label on this surface; a display refresh cadence, not business behavior.

entries.name: SLOW_LOAD_NOTICE_MS
entries.reason: Patience threshold before a loading skeleton admits it is taking a while; explicitly documented in the source as 'a constant here and not a knob'.

entries.name: IDENTITY_RETRY_DELAY_MS
entries.reason: Retry delay paired with the identity-settle budget above; resilience plumbing.

entries.name: IDENTITY_SETTLE_BUDGET_MS
entries.reason: How long an error-capture flush waits for the browser to acquire any identity before giving up on recording; a boot-race resilience budget, not a business setting.

entries.name: WRITE_DEBOUNCE_MS
entries.reason: Debounce before mirroring a text field's draft into sessionStorage; the same interaction-feel pattern used by other editors in this codebase.

entries.name: BULK_RESOLVE_PAGE_SIZE
entries.reason: Explicitly documented in the source as 'a transport batch, not a product limit (so not a knob)'; resolution always continues to the server's own real total regardless of this value.

entries.name: DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE
entries.reason: Explicitly matches PostgREST's own db-max-rows ceiling on Matrx Main, which this paging logic exists to page past.

entries.name: RESOLUTION_TIMEOUT_MS
entries.reason: Bounded wait for the organization-bootstrap answer before a write refuses anyway, so a stuck promise can never hang forever; a resilience timeout.

entries.name: MINUTE_MS
entries.reason: A literal unit-conversion constant (milliseconds per minute) used to build a progress sentence; not a configurable behavior at all.

entries.name: MAX_PENDING_POLLS
entries.reason: Explicitly a computed backoff-schedule length (source comment: '1+2+4+8 then 19x15 seconds: five visible minutes'); an engineering-derived constant, not a knob.

entries.name: MAX_TRANSPORT_FAILURES
entries.reason: How many consecutive sandbox-transport failures are tolerated before giving up; an engineering reliability threshold, not a business setting.

entries.name: MAX_RACE_RETRIES
entries.reason: How many times a knob read retries after losing a race with a concurrent write; a cache-consistency bug fix, not a business setting.

entries.name: IDB_OPERATION_TIMEOUT_MS
entries.reason: Timeout on a single IndexedDB operation so a blocked browser request can never hang sync forever; browser-storage plumbing.

entries.name: GOOGLE_IDENTITY_POLL_INTERVAL_MS
entries.reason: Paired poll-interval constant explicitly covered by the same 'not an organization knob' documentation as the readiness timeout beside it.

entries.name: GOOGLE_IDENTITY_READY_TIMEOUT_MS
entries.reason: Explicitly documented in the source as a CAPS constant and NOT an organization knob: a technical readiness limit on how long Google's third-party sign-in script can plausibly take to load.

entries.name: SESSION_ATTACH_BUDGET_MS
entries.reason: How long a request may wait for the first auth report before proceeding anyway; a resilience budget, not a business setting.

entries.name: SESSION_RECOVERY_BUDGET_MS
entries.reason: How long a refused request may wait for a session before giving up; paired resilience budget with the attach budget.

entries.name: WAIT_COOLDOWN_MS
entries.reason: How long every other request skips the session wait after one wait already expired; a cooldown to avoid repeatedly paying the same budget, not a business setting.
